2608.06917.title: ReGraph: Learning to Generate Recipe Graphs from Food Images
2608.06917.paper_summary: Recent Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) have achieved impressive performance in recipe generation from food images.However, cooking is a structured transformation process in which ingredients undergo state changes through ordered actions,while free-form recipe language leaves the corresponding entities, intermediate states, and dependencies largely implicit and entangled.A graph representation makes this procedural knowledge explicit and compositional, providing a structured basis for assessing whether model outputs encode process-level knowledge rather than merely presenting plausible textual descriptions. To address this limitation, we present ReGraph, a large-scale recipe graph dataset that represents ingredients, cooking actions, and tools as entities, uses entity attributes to describe ingredient state changes, and employs typed relations to encode manipulation targets, destinations, and procedural ordering. ReGraph further incorporates explicit Recipe Reasoning Chain-of-Thought (RR-CoT) traces, providing auxiliary supervision for procedural decomposition and structured graph generation. Building on ReGraph, we propose Recipe Graph Learning (RGL), a two-stage framework that enables LMMs to generate a plausible fine-grained cooking workflow from a food image in the form of a structured recipe graph. Under a deterministic, schema-aware matching protocol, our experiments reveal a substantial gap between text-generation quality and recoverable procedural structure: recipes produced by existing approaches achieve competitive text-generation scores yet yield limited reference-aligned entity and relation structure under the ReGraph schema. In contrast, across two representative LMM backbones, RGL consistently improves the generation of cooking entities and procedural relations, while our analysis further shows that fine-grained ingredient-state capture remains the most challenging dimension.
2608.06917.paper_summary_zh: 最近的大型多模態模型（LMMs）在從食物圖像生成食譜方面取得了令人印象深刻的表現。<lb/>然而，烹飪是一個結構化的轉換過程，其中成分通過有序的動作經歷狀態變化，而自由形式的食譜語言則使得相應的實體、中間狀態和依賴關係在很大程度上隱含且糾纏不清。<lb/>圖形表示使這種程序性知識變得明確且可組合，為評估模型輸出是否編碼過程級知識而非僅僅呈現合理的文本描述提供了結構化的基礎。<lb/>為了解決這一限制，我們提出了ReGraph，一個大型食譜圖數據集，將成分、烹飪動作和工具表示為實體，使用實體屬性來描述成分狀態變化，並利用類型化關係來編碼操作目標、目的地和程序排序。<lb/>ReGraph進一步納入了明確的食譜推理鏈思維（RR-CoT）痕跡，為程序分解和結構化圖生成提供輔助監督。<lb/>基於ReGraph，我們提出了食譜圖學習（RGL），一個兩階段框架，使LMMs能夠從食物圖像生成一個合理的細粒度烹飪工作流程，形式為結構化的食譜圖。<lb/>在一個確定性、模式感知的匹配協議下，我們的實驗揭示了文本生成質量與可恢復程序結構之間的顯著差距：現有方法生成的食譜在文本生成分數上具有競爭力，但在ReGraph模式下產生的參考對齊實體和關係結構有限。<lb/>相比之下，在兩個具有代表性的LMM骨幹中，RGL始終改善了烹飪實體和程序關係的生成，而我們的分析進一步顯示，細粒度的成分狀態捕捉仍然是最具挑戰性的維度。
